newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A labour leader has been arrested during a protest by 500 workers laid off by three companies at the Labour and Social Welfare Ministry. Chin Thapplee, vice-president of the National Assembly of Labour Congresses, and six colleagues, are accused of blocking a road to the Thai Kobe Welding Co plant in Samut Prakan province with burning tyres on September 15, 1993. A warrant for Chin's arrest for inciting unrest was issued by a police station in the province. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Metropolitan Police chief has assigned a senior officer to find ways to close permanently the Taurus Pub in the wake of a recent shooting. The order follows a raid in which police found the floor littered with drugs, such as ecstasy, and the May 27 shooting in which the son of Chatchawal Kong-udom, an influential figure, was charged with attempted murder. (BANGKOK POST)

- Four major political parties from both sides of the House have joined forces to oppose the new charter's proposal requiring members of parliament to resign before becoming Cabinet members, an issue which could prompt many politicians to vote against the draft. (THE NATION)

- A new era is dawning for Thailand's oil refining industry after the government this week resolved to dismantle all barriers to the establishment and expansion of oil refineries in Thailand. The decision by the National Energy Policy Committee on Monday means all parties are free to set up new refineries or increase their production capacities without having to painstakingly seek special government permission. (BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan will meet with representatives from the Thai Bankers Association to seek their cooperation in bringing down interest rates on home loans. The meeting is planned in the wake of a highly successful measure by the government to provide low-interest home loans. (BUSINESS DAY) (THE NATION)
